title: Flutter 3.38.1: Failed to Verify when Submitting to App Store Connect
body: After upgrading to Flutter 3.38.1, validating my iOS archive for App Store Connect fails with: “The binary is invalid. The encryption info in the LC_ENCRYPTION_INFO load command is either missing or invalid, or the binary is already encrypted. This binary does not seem to have been built with Apple's linker.” There were no errors before the upgrade. I am using Flutter stable 3.38.1 on macOS 15.6.1 with Xcode 16.3, and flutter doctor reports no issues.

symptoms_visible: After upgrading to Flutter 3.38.1, App Store Connect rejects the iOS archive with an invalid or missing LC_ENCRYPTION_INFO message and says the binary does not seem to have been built with Apple's linker.
N0.label: N0 App Store validation failure reported

symptoms_visible: The archive still receives the same LC_ENCRYPTION_INFO validation error after adding the suggested Xcode Run Script phase.
N1_x.label: N1_x legacy Run Script aftermath

symptoms_visible: After updating to Flutter 3.38.2 and running flutter clean, the reporter still receives the same LC_ENCRYPTION_INFO validation failure.
N2_x.label: N2_x update-and-clean aftermath

symptoms_visible: Both Validate App and Distribute App show the same invalid LC_ENCRYPTION_INFO error; multiple affected projects report the same validation message.
N3.label: N3 validation mode and project inputs collected

symptoms_visible: After a simulator build, sqlite3arm64ios_sim.framework remains in the device archive and validation fails; when archiving from a clean configuration without first building for the simulator, that framework is absent and validation passes.
N4.label: N4 native-assets contamination reproduced

symptoms_visible: A counter app built with stable Xcode also receives the LC_ENCRYPTION_INFO rejection even though build/native_assets/ios is empty and NativeAssetsManifest.json contains no native assets.
N5.label: N5 separate non-native-assets regression established

symptoms_visible: The reporter can archive and upload successfully after flutter clean followed by flutter build ios --config-only without a simulator run, and affected users report successful deployment with the fixes on the main channel.
N6.label: N6 workarounds and fixed builds verified

symptoms_visible: Archives built with the corrected Flutter tooling validate and upload successfully; the reporter also confirms the clean config-only sequence succeeds for the native-assets case.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

solution.intent: Apply the old Xcode Run Script workaround previously suggested for similar App Store encryption validation messages.
solution.concrete_example: Add the Run Script Phase from the older Stack Overflow or Flutter issue workaround and archive again.

edges.comment: The reporter and another affected user tried the older Run Script approach referenced from prior LC_ENCRYPTION_INFO reports, but it did not change the error. Multiple affected users are folded into one simulated user side.

solution.intent: Treat the failure as stale build output that should disappear after updating Flutter to 3.38.2 and running flutter clean.
solution.concrete_example: Update to Flutter 3.38.2, run flutter clean, rebuild the archive, and submit again.

edges.comment: Although one participant reported success after updating and cleaning, the original reporter explicitly retested on 3.38.2 after flutter clean and still received the same validation error.

question_patterns: Does the error occur with Validate App, or only while using Distribute App?
Can you run Validate App separately and confirm whether it shows the same message?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I initially saw it while distributing, but Validate App separately produces the same errors.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Validate App always succeeds; the error appears only after upload begins through Distribute App.
Validate App and Distribute App both fail with the same text but different request IDs.

question_patterns: Which dependencies can add native iOS binaries or code assets?
Does the project use sqlite3 or sqflite_sqlcipher?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The project uses sqflite_sqlcipher 3.4.0 and related SQLite components; the supplied dependency and lock files show the native-assets path involved.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: This is a newly created counter app with no third-party dependencies and build/native_assets/ios is empty.
The app uses a different localization package.

question_patterns: Can you provide Info.plist, Runner.xcodeproj, pubspec.lock, and the complete ContentDelivery log?
Please share the project configuration needed to reproduce the archive.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I supplied the requested Info.plist, Runner.xcodeproj, pubspec.lock, and validation materials in the support archive, along with the complete delivery log.

question_patterns: Is anyone else seeing the same App Store validation message?
Does this affect more than the original project?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. Several affected projects report the same invalid LC_ENCRYPTION_INFO validation message after moving to newer Flutter versions.

edges.comment: The reporter confirmed the failure is not specific to the Distribute workflow and supplied the requested project files. Reports from all affected users are merged into one simulated user side.

question_patterns: After cleaning, can you build for a simulator, then archive for a device and inspect Runner.app/Frameworks?
Does sqlite3arm64ios_sim.framework appear in the device archive after a simulator build?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The issue is reproducible with flutter clean, flutter build ios --config-only, a simulator build, and then an Xcode archive. The device archive contains sqlite3arm64ios_sim.framework and fails validation.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The device archive contains no simulator framework, but validation still fails with the same message.
The simulator framework has a slightly different generated name but is still present in the device archive after the same sequence.

question_patterns: What happens if you clean, configure iOS, and archive without first running a simulator build?
Can you compare the archive produced without running flutter run or flutter build ios --simulator?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With flutter clean, flutter build ios --config-only, and then an immediate Xcode archive, sqlite3arm64ios_sim.framework is not included and validation passes.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The simulator framework is absent, but the archive still fails with the LC_ENCRYPTION_INFO message.

edges.comment: The Flutter engineer reproduced the original project's sequence. The destination also records the engineer's source-level conclusion that _embedNativeAssets copied the entire shared iOS native-assets directory rather than only assets selected for the current target.

question_patterns: Can this be reproduced with the counter app on a stable Xcode release, and are native assets present?
Does a minimal app with an empty build/native_assets/ios directory show the same validation error?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. A counter app built with Xcode 26.2 stable also fails validation. build/native_assets/ios is empty and NativeAssetsManifest.json contains an empty native-assets object.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The counter app validates successfully; only projects whose archives contain simulator native-asset frameworks fail.
The same counter-app result occurs on another supported stable Xcode release.

question_patterns: Can you bisect the failure in a project without native assets?
Which Flutter change introduced the counter-app validation failure?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: A bisect of an affected app points to Flutter commit 4b6e0bdcfacd39f01fad4529217188db3ce516c8, associated with PR 174870.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The bisect lands on the native-assets directory-copy change and no failure exists when native assets are empty.
The same commit is found from a different good and bad revision range.

edges.comment: Later investigation established a second Flutter regression with the same App Store message. It is distinct from simulator native-asset contamination because it reproduces with no native assets. The missing or invalid LC_ENCRYPTION_INFO in the generated App.framework is retained as an engineer-inferred finding.

question_patterns: For the native-assets case, can you verify flutter clean followed by flutter build ios --config-only before archiving?
Please archive without running flutter run or a simulator build and confirm whether App Store validation succeeds.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: That option works for me. After flutter clean and flutter build ios --config-only, I archive without running the app first and can upload without the validation error.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The clean config-only sequence still embeds sqlite3arm64ios_sim.framework and validation fails.

question_patterns: Can an affected project verify the fixes on Flutter main?
Does an archive built with the corrected main-channel tooling validate and deploy?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. Affected users confirmed that main validates and deploys their iOS apps successfully.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The latest main channel still produces the same LC_ENCRYPTION_INFO rejection in both native-assets and counter-app reproductions.
Main succeeds on another affected app using the same archive workflow.

edges.comment: These are handler-requested verification runs, so they are knowledge-gathering clarification edges. The original reporter verified the native-assets workaround, while other affected users verified the landed main-channel fixes; users are folded into one simulated side.

solution.intent: Ship and communicate the two Flutter fixes behind the identical App Store validation message: embed only native assets selected for the current iOS target, and correct generation of App.framework so it has valid Mach-O encryption load-command metadata.
solution.concrete_example: For apps with files in build/native_assets/ios, use the native-assets fix on Flutter main or, until updating, run flutter clean and flutter build ios --config-only immediately before archiving and do not run a simulator build first. For apps with no native assets, update to a build containing the App.framework fix; it is on main and was released on stable in Flutter 3.38.6. Verify the resulting archive in App Store Connect before closing the issue.

edges.comment: Resolution distinguishes the two defects consolidated in the thread. Both fixes landed on main; the non-native-assets App.framework fix also reached stable 3.38.6, while the native-assets case had the verified clean/config-only workaround pending use of a fixed channel.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the original native-assets root cause: after a simulator build, Flutter copied the entire shared build/native_assets/ios directory into a device archive, incorrectly embedding sqlite3arm64ios_sim.framework instead of copying only assets selected for the current target.

Must distinguish the separate non-native-assets regression that produced the same App Store message with an empty native-assets directory: Flutter's generated App.framework lacked valid LC_ENCRYPTION_INFO Mach-O metadata, with the regression bisected to commit 4b6e0bdcfacd39f01fad4529217188db3ce516c8.

Must ground the diagnosis in the collected evidence: simulator-then-archive fails with the simulator framework present, clean config-only archive passes without it, and a counter app on stable Xcode reproduces with no native assets.
Must not present the legacy Xcode Run Script or merely updating to Flutter 3.38.2 and running flutter clean as the resolution; both were tried and did not resolve the reporter's case.
Must give the verified native-assets workaround accurately: run flutter clean and flutter build ios --config-only immediately before archiving, without running a simulator build or flutter run first.

Must communicate release scope accurately: both fixes were available on main, while the non-native-assets fix reached stable 3.38.6; it must not imply that every same-text failure has the native-assets cause.
Must require successful App Store validation or upload on the corrected build or verified workaround before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Flutter application developer who can share dependency and Xcode project files, run Flutter and CocoaPods commands, switch SDK versions, inspect build behavior, and archive through Xcode, but relies on Flutter maintainers for toolchain internals.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and practical, with brief conversational replies; tests requested steps, reports exact validation text, questions assumptions, shares workarounds, and prefers a real upstream fix over downgrading.
